label: POOL Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct GPTQ-INT4, --max-num-batched-tokens sweep (companion to baseline-pool-llama31-70b-concurrency.json)
verdict: Open item 4 is REFUTED, in the direction opposite to the one it assumed. Raising --max-num-batched-tokens does not help this pool -- it hurts twice. Going 2048 -> 4096 made a 4k-token prefill 28% slower AND cost 20% of the KV cache. Going the other way pays twice: 2048 -> 512 made the same prefill 22% faster and bought 13% more KV, with no loss of short-prompt decode throughput. The cause is pipeline overlap: prefill is split into chunks of max_num_batched_tokens, and on a 2-stage pipeline chunk k+1 occupies stage 0 while chunk k occupies stage 1. A bigger prefill batch means FEWER chunks and therefore LESS overlap.
topology: vLLM 0.29.0, --pipeline-parallel-size 2, ray backend, desktop RTX 3090 sm_86 (PP0) + laptop RTX 5090 sm_120 (PP1) over direct 2.5GbE

method.design: Four full pool restarts, one per value of --max-num-batched-tokens (B). Predictions for B=4096 and B=1024 were written down BEFORE the first restart (scratch file predictions.md) and are reproduced under `preregistered_predictions`; both landed inside their stated range.
method.probe: bench/prefill_curve.py -- single stream, max_tokens 8 so the measurement is dominated by prefill, TTFT taken from the first streamed content chunk, 3 samples per length, prompts rebuilt from freshly drawn unique random 4-digit numbers for every sample so prefix caching can never serve one.
method.decode_probe: bench/bench.py (unchanged) at c=5 repeats=6 (150 samples) and c=16 repeats=2 (160 samples), plus bench/conc_probe.py for long prompts under concurrency with ignore_eos so every request emits exactly 128 tokens.
method.control: The B=2048 curve was measured on the instance that had been up for 13 h before any restart, and its numbers reproduce the recorded regime C of the concurrency baseline (marginal 505-572 tok/s below 2048, ~1050 above). The pool was returned to B=2048 at the end and re-measured: 2.72/2.41 GiB and 3.86x, identical to the state it was found in.
method.tokenization_note: This probe's separator makes a 4-digit number cost ~4.05 tokens, not the 3.07 of the concurrency baseline's probe (different formatting). All lengths here are the API's own usage.prompt_tokens, so the two files' x-axes are directly comparable even though their number counts are not.

preregistered_predictions.model_under_test: Prefill is chunked at B; on a 2-stage pipeline every chunk after the first is served at roughly twice the single-chunk rate, so fewer chunks means less overlap.
preregistered_predictions.B_4096: one chunk for any prompt <= 3950 tokens, so no knee and a straight line at ~500-570 tok/s; TTFT at ~3950 tokens 7.4-7.8 s
preregistered_predictions.B_4096_outcome: CONFIRMED. No knee; marginal rate fell monotonically 573 -> 474 tok/s. TTFT 7.810 s.
preregistered_predictions.B_1024: knee moves from 2048 to 1024; marginal rate above 1024 ~900-1100 tok/s; TTFT at ~3950 tokens 4.6-5.4 s
preregistered_predictions.B_1024_outcome: CONFIRMED. Knee at 1024 (1170->1350 jumped to 1070 tok/s). TTFT 5.158 s.

kv_cost_of_the_prefill_batch.note: Two figures per row because the stages are not symmetric; the SMALLER one binds, and the engine's 'Maximum concurrency' line is that stage's token budget divided by max_model_len.

rows.note: the engine default here, and the configuration every earlier baseline was taken at

kv_cost_of_the_prefill_batch.finding: KV is monotonically decreasing in B: each doubling of the prefill batch takes activation memory out of the KV budget, and the loss accelerates (512->2048 costs 0.33 GiB, 2048->4096 costs another 0.48). So B trades directly against the concurrency ceiling established in the companion file, where ceiling = kv_tokens / (prompt_tokens + max_tokens).

prefill_curves.units: TTFT seconds, median of 3 cold samples; spread within a length was under 1% at every point except the smallest
prefill_curves.finding: The knee tracks B exactly. At B=4096 there is no knee at all and the marginal rate decays monotonically from 573 to 474 tok/s -- the pure single-chunk curve, with one pipeline stage always idle. At every smaller B the marginal rate roughly doubles once the prompt passes B, which is the second chunk overlapping the first. This is the direct causal test the companion file called for: the boundary is not a property of the model or of 2048, it MOVES when the flag moves.

decode_throughput_is_unaffected.method: bench/bench.py, identical invocation at both batch sizes, on this session's instances.
decode_throughput_is_unaffected.finding: No effect, in either direction, on short-prompt decode. The prefill batch does not bind when prompts are 18-40 tokens. The wall-clock and standard-deviation spread seen at B=512 (221.8 s, sd 3.2) is NOT a 512 effect: the restored default reproduced it (219.3 s, sd 3.2) against its own earlier 189.1 s / sd 1.8. Run-to-run, not configuration.

long_prompts_under_concurrency.method: bench/conc_probe.py, unique random prompts per run, min_tokens = max_tokens = 128 with ignore_eos so every request emits exactly 128 tokens. Runs repeated 2-3x per cell; repeats agreed within 1% except where noted.
long_prompts_under_concurrency.finding: B=512 buys 20-30% off TTFT and 8-11% on aggregate throughput, and pays 3-8% of per-request decode rate. The trade is worth taking for any long-prompt workload: the decode loss is smaller than the TTFT gain and the aggregate moves the right way. Note the 3857-token rows sit against a KV cliff -- 3857+128 = 3985 tokens per request, so at B=2048 (15,808 KV tokens) only 3.97 fit and the fourth request queues for the whole run, while at B=512 (17,940) all four fit. That cliff is a consequence of B, not a confound, but it does mean the size of the c=4 gap is specific to this prompt length.

high_concurrency_short_prompts_at_512.why: The one regime the sweep had not covered before 512 became bin/lab's default: the 70B's peak-throughput workload, 128 concurrent short requests. The 2048 figures are the c=128 row of baseline-pool-llama31-70b-concurrency.json.
high_concurrency_short_prompts_at_512.instance: Fresh 'lab pool up' with POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS UNSET, so bin/lab's new default supplied it; the log's non-default args show 'max_num_batched_tokens': 512. KV 3.04 GiB desktop / 2.58 GiB laptop, 16,912 tokens, 4.13x.
high_concurrency_short_prompts_at_512.method: bench/bench.py --concurrency 128 --repeats 1 --max-tokens 128 (640 samples, the same invocation as the 2048 row), after one throwaway request. server_side = median of the 'Avg generation throughput' 10 s windows with Running >= 100 (13 windows; mean 523.6 is dragged down by the ramp-up window). Board power sampled at 1 Hz on both nodes with nvidia-smi.
preregistered: Written 2026-09-23T19:15:21-06:00, before the c=128 run at B=512.
per-request p50 4.632, aggregate 592.9 derived / 601.6 server, TTFT p50 0.776 p95 2.608,
1. Engine reports ~2.74 GiB binding-stage KV and ~4.38x (reproduces last session's B=512 instance).
2. Aggregate within +/-5% of baseline: derived 563-623, server 572-632. Reason: ~64 decode
tokens per microbatch at c=128, far under 512; prompts are 18-40 tokens, mostly prefix-cached.
3. Waiting max 0; KV peak BELOW 90.7% (bigger KV pool).
4. TTFT p50 within noise; p95 same or higher (initial 128-request burst prefills in narrower chunks).
Decision rule: aggregate >5% below baseline => do NOT conclude; run a same-day B=2048 control first.

outcomes.1_kv: MISSED. 4.13x, not ~4.38x. The desktop stage gained as expected (3.04 GiB); the laptop stage came up ~160 MiB short of the 2026-09-22 512 instance (2.58 vs 2.74 GiB). Still 7% more KV than the 2048 instance it replaced (16,912 vs 15,808 tokens). Cause unconfirmed. vLLM charges any device-wide memory growth during its load to its own overhead (vllm/utils/mem_utils.py: cuda_memory = total - free), so another GPU client on the laptop's display card can shrink KV silently; but the only new client found, a Files window (65 MiB), launched 42 s before ray-worker started, which argues against it.
outcomes.2_aggregate: CONFIRMED. +0.4% derived, -2.8% server-side, both inside +/-5%. The control-run rule did not trigger.
outcomes.3_queueing: CONFIRMED. Waiting 0 throughout; KV peak 85.2% against 90.7%.
outcomes.4_ttft: PARTLY. p95 unchanged (2.598 vs 2.608 s). p50 rose 10% (0.852 vs 0.776 s), which was not predicted. Likely mechanism: bench.py runs at temperature 0, so the 128 copies of a prompt finish together and their replacements arrive as one wave, whose prefill takes several 512-token steps instead of one 2048-token step. The server log shows the waves: generation dips to 437-446 tok/s in the windows where prompt throughput jumps to 117-156. 76 ms on requests that take ~28 s. One run, no same-day control.

high_concurrency_short_prompts_at_512.verdict: 512 costs nothing measurable at the 70B's peak-throughput workload.

power_w.note: GPU board power only; wall draw is higher. ~0.73 J per generated token at c=128 (429 W / ~590 tok/s). The laptop spent 32 of 162 s at >= 80 C, peaking at 82 C, under bench.py's 83 C poison line. At c=128 the laptop, not the desktop, was the hotter card.

recommendation.setting: POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS=512 for 70B pooled serving. Short-prompt traffic is indifferent to it (measured at c=5, 16 and 128).
recommendation.caution: This is measured on a 2-stage PIPELINE. The mechanism is stage overlap, so it should NOT be generalised to a single-node or tensor-parallel deployment, where chunking buys nothing and a bigger batch is the usual advice. vLLM's own tuning guide recommends >8192 for throughput; that guidance assumes no pipeline cut.
recommendation.applied: 2026-09-23: bin/lab now defaults POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS to 512, with the comment block rewritten around stage overlap; set 2048 explicitly to get vLLM's own resolution back. The 14B is untested at 512 and the comment says so.

open.b_256_untested: 512 is the smallest value measured and it was still improving (2048->1024 gained 15.2%, 1024->512 a further 8.2%, so 256 might gain ~4%). It was not tested: 256 equals this deployment's resolved max_num_seqs, and colliding those two limits would confound the measurement.
open.qwen3_14b_not_retested: The whole sweep is 70B-only. The 14B pool is bubble-bound rather than weight-bound, so the overlap argument probably applies to it too, but that is inference, not measurement.
open.laptop_kv_shortfall: The 2026-09-23 512 instance's laptop stage had ~160 MiB less KV than the 2026-09-22 one (see high_concurrency_short_prompts_at_512.outcomes.1_kv). Unexplained; only one instance of each.

traps_found.fixed_seed_prefix_cache: The first version of conc_probe.py seeded its RNG with a constant, so every run sent byte-identical prompts and the prefix cache served them: TTFT collapsed from 10.4 s to 0.2 s and aggregate throughput doubled to 116 tok/s. An entire first round of B=512 vs B=2048 comparisons was void because one side ran warm and the other cold. The probe now seeds from the clock. This is the same artifact the companion file documents for bench.py's fixed prompt set -- it is easy to walk into twice.
traps_found.cold_start_outlier: The first request after 'lab pool up' is not representative: a c=4 full-context probe took 65.7 s wall on a freshly started engine against 33.6 s steady-state. Send one throwaway request after pool up before measuring anything.
traps_found.small_sample_p50_at_c5: bench.py at c=5 with 50 samples reported a decode p50 of 15.440 tok/s in one run and 19.2 in others -- the distribution is bimodal there and 50 samples is too few to place the median. At 150 samples it is stable at 19.14-19.22. Do not read a single 50-sample c=5 run as a regression.
traps_found.bench_py_temp_is_a_spot_read: bench.py's temp_max is read once, at the end of each pass. At c=128 it reported 60 C while 1 Hz sampling saw 82 C: the last seconds of a pass run only the stragglers, and a laptop card cools fast. Sample continuously when temperature matters.

provenance.restarts: 5 pool restarts (4096, 1024, 512, default, and a second default after the 512 battery). Each 'lab pool up' took 1m49s-3m47s. Plus one on 2026-09-23 for the c=128 check, 'lab pool up' with the variable unset.
provenance.final_state: 2026-09-23: pool left UP on bin/lab's 512 default (POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS unset), 3.04/2.58 GiB KV, 4.13x, serving at http://10.10.0.1:8200/v1
